versions.short: The bill would transfer about 9.89 acres of former Albuquerque Indian School federal land, now under the General Services Administration, into federal trust for the benefit of the 19 Pueblos of New Mexico. It would require the Administrator of General Services to hand administrative control of the land to the Interior Department within 90 days, and the Interior Secretary would then place it in trust within a further 90 days. The land would be used for educational, health, cultural, business, and economic development of the Pueblos, and it would remain subject to existing private, municipal, and utility rights. The bill would also transfer ownership of the buildings and improvements on the land to the Indian Pueblo Cultural Center, with a lease letting current federal tenants stay on one tract for an initial term of up to 24 months. Finally, the land could not be used for class II or class III gaming.
